headline: Benchmarking and uncertainty-aware modeling of sequencing variant detection
label: Genomic Variant Detection Methods
summary: Recent preprints and a published study address error control and uncertainty in variant calling, effect estimation, and read processing.
synthesis: The shared thread is quantitative control of error and uncertainty across the variant detection pipeline. A DNA reference-mixture benchmark of targeted and whole-exome sequencing tunes DRAGEN's recurrent false-positive allele filtering and VAF thresholds to maximize sensitivity and specificity. NanoSimFormer addresses the same problem through simulation: a Transformer-based nanopore signal simulator trained with basecaller guidance that reproduces human variant calling and bacterial assembly. Lilace contributes Bayesian estimation of variant effects with explicit uncertainty quantification from FACS-based deep mutational scanning. Y-Trim is adjacent, handling read-level trimming of Adaptase tails in ssWGBS by separating trim admission from cut placement. What is new is the combination of simulation-based and uncertainty-aware estimation applied across sequencing modalities, from benchmarking to effect inference.
